verdict.summary: SPEC-0336: base names git refuses are now caught at validate, a signal between checkout and the slot stage gives an error frame (stage signal, exit 3), one broken cache no longer stops gc for later repos (new `errors` key, CLI exits 1), and the budget tests no longer depend on wall-clock margins.
tests_run: uv run pytest -q -n {4,6,8,4,6} tests/test_worker.py tests/test_worker_ssh_command.py tests/test_gate_slots.py tests/test_cli_gate_slots.py tests/test_agentic_gates.py tests/test_rich_output_guard.py tests/test_test_waits.py (213 passed each of 5 runs; one more full run of the set also passed)
with the src/ diff reverse-applied: the new signal, broken-cache and 6 base-name cases fail (they test the fixes)

ac_status.ac: valid header+bundle runs gates; accepted/started/gate/done frames
env outside allowlist -> validate error; reused job_id -> claim
concurrent jobs with different base.sha see own base
EOF mid-gate / during slot wait -> done interrupted
log over 16 MiB truncated with truncated_bytes
have after job; gc --keep-days 0 removes refs/objects/dirs except live job
ssh-command execs four allowed subcommands, refuses rest with exit 2
WORKFLOW.md documents mandatory dedicated user and key line

followup_ideas: The older base-name refusal cases (`../main`, `-main`) were only passing because env.NW_BASE stayed `main`, so the NW_BASE mismatch check refused them first. They are now set through a helper that changes both fields. Other header-refusal parametrizations may hide the same problem and are worth an audit.

gate_slots.acquire takes a free slot even when stop= is already set, so a job cancelled just before the slot stage emits `started` before `done` interrupted. Worth deciding whether acquire should check stop first.
